meta.structure: Each profileId maps to { monthlyWeight: number[12], dayTypes: { summer: {weekday, weekend}, winter: {weekday, weekend} } }. monthlyWeight[m] is the month's average daily energy relative to the annual average daily energy (sums to 12 across the year). Each dayTypes.<season>.<weekday|weekend> array is a 24-value fractional-of-day template (index 0 = hour 00:00-01:00 local standard time through index 23 = 23:00-24:00) that sums to 1.0. To reconstruct an hourly kWh value: hourly_kWh = dailyAverage_kWh * monthlyWeight[month] * dayTypeTemplate[hourOfDay], where dailyAverage_kWh is the annual average daily energy. Season definitions follow PG&E's rate-season convention: summer = Jun-Sep, winter = Oct-May. weekend = Saturday/Sunday; weekday = Monday-Friday (US federal holidays are not separately broken out).

profiles.residential: Derived from PG&E's E-1 (residential default) dynamic load profile, 10-year average 2015-2024. Shows the Central Valley summer evening air-conditioning peak (~5-9pm, hours 17-20) and a flatter winter shape with morning (7-8am) and evening (7-8pm) bumps.
profiles.small-commercial: Derived from PG&E's A-1 (small commercial/industrial general service) dynamic load profile, 10-year average 2015-2024. Shows a daytime office-hours shape peaking early-to-mid afternoon (2-3pm) with a shallow weekend usage.

sources.title: PG&E Dynamic Load Profiles - E-1 (Residential)
sources.note: Actual hourly load-profile index values by date for the E-1 rate class, 2000-present. Averaged here over 2015-2024 (3,287 days), split by PG&E summer/winter rate season and weekday/weekend, then normalized to a unit-sum 24-hour template.

sources.title: PG&E Dynamic Load Profiles - A-1 (Small Commercial)
sources.note: Same methodology as above, applied to the A-1 rate class as the small-commercial reference shape.

sources.title: PG&E Instruction for Using Static/Dynamic Load Profiles
sources.note: Landing page describing PG&E load profile methodology and rate class definitions.

sources.title: NREL End-Use Load Profiles for the U.S. Building Stock
sources.note: Referenced for cross-checking qualitative residential shape characteristics (summer evening AC peak, winter dual morning/evening bump); not used as a numeric source because the raw hourly dataset was not directly retrievable in this environment.

sources.title: DOE Commercial Reference Buildings (Small Office) load-shape benchmarking
sources.note: Referenced for cross-checking the small-office/small-commercial daytime shape (rise ~8am, peak early-mid afternoon, fall ~6pm); the numeric template used is the PG&E A-1 profile above.

meta.generatedNote: monthlyWeight values are rounded to 4 decimals and re-summed to exactly 12 (adjustment applied to December). Day-type template values are rounded to 6 decimals and re-summed to exactly 1.0 (adjustment applied to the last hour, 23:00-24:00).
